tasks.short: Supervise editing, assembly and recording staff

steps.what: Supervise and coordinate workers engaged in film editing, assembling and recording activities

tasks.design: Retain supervision and coordination with the editor, using existing {PROJECT} records and {TELEPHONY} conversations. A visible task list supports discussion without replacing workload judgement or coaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Priorities, creative dependencies and staff needs change during production.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project records already support coordination; no new labour-saving step is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: An updated status does not resolve a creative disagreement or unrealistic deadline.
tasks.human_edge: Balance production needs, individual capability and the quality of the edit.
tasks.altitude: Supervisory time and authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Substantive staff supervision and production coordination remain human work; the digest's editing features do not establish savings here.

assumptions: Boundary is focal editor supervision and coordination, not other workers' execution or a separately invented scheduling task. Existing team participation remains outside and unchanged.

Editor obtains current versions, priorities, dependencies and staff constraints during retained100 hours before assigning or revising work. Team members produce progress information as work occurs and discuss blockers before decisions. No free structured-ready or capacity flag is assumed; uncertainty prompts direct clarification.
Native project records precede custom automation; existing notifications and runtime create no new saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because process and tools are unchanged.
research_questions: Which coordination issues require discussion even when project status is current?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Coaching and resolving production dependencies retain their time; no separate administrative baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine specific audio and visual effects and music necessary to complete films

tasks.design: Keep the choice of necessary effects and music with the editor viewing the current cut in {OTHER}. Record requirements in {DOCS} for discussion with the production team.
tasks.previous_blocker: An effect's value depends on the film's purpose, tone and timing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing playback and asset information support decisions; no new creative capability is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: A technically possible effect may distract from the story or imply the wrong tone.
tasks.human_edge: Know when an effect or music cue helps and when silence or simplicity is better.
tasks.altitude: Creative judgement and decision time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess technical feasibility of proposed cues

evidence.claim: Choosing effects and music is retained creative judgement; the digest's rough-cut and transcript-editing capabilities do not establish a saving in this choice.

assumptions: OTHER means a video editing application. Boundary is determining requirements, not generating assets, licensing, sound discussion4071 or inserting them under4052. Overlapping creative decisions are assigned once in roll-ups.

Editor produces cut/version reference, cue location, intended effect, timing, alternatives and unresolved asset constraints within retained100 hours. Production supplies current cut and creative intent before related choices; no free approved-cue or rights-cleared flag is assumed. Missing asset information prompts manual clarification.
Native playback and asset search precede custom tools; no synthetic media generation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new process or tool is introduced.
research_questions: Which requirements are creative choices rather than repeat asset lookup?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Effects/music judgement retains time; generation or insertion savings are outside this task.

steps.what: Prepare the correct film version and verify screening playback
Conduct film screenings for directors and production staffs and discuss their reactions

tasks.design: Retain screening setup checks and the shared viewing in the playback equipment in {OTHER}. The editor helps the director and staff interpret the cut and clarify feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shared viewing and discussion are the purpose of the task.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing playback supports screening; no new automation gain is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Feedback can conflict or refer to a different version of the film.
tasks.human_edge: Understand reactions and clarify the intended change without losing creative context.
tasks.altitude: Screening responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Conducting a screening retains shared viewing and discussion; no digest source establishes a shorter screening session.

assumptions: OTHER means screening playback equipment. Boundary is setup, screening and immediate clarification, not separate calendar booking or subsequent editing. Existing participants' attendance is outside focal time and unchanged.

Editor verifies exact file/version, picture/sound tracks and playback settings during s1's20 hours before s2. Director and staff produce reactions during s2 before feedback is clarified. No pre-existing screening-ready or approved-feedback flag is assumed; playback faults use normal manual troubleshooting.
Native playback precedes custom workflows; existing render/playback runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the screening process is unchanged.
research_questions: Are setup faults or version mismatches affecting screening quality without changing the viewing duration?

already_counted.description: Playback setup checks, screening and feedback clarification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Setup checks and shared viewing retain time; unattended playback is not labour saved.

tasks.short: Discuss sound requirements with effects editors

steps.what: Discuss the sound requirements of pictures with sound effects editors

tasks.design: Retain the sound discussion through {TELEPHONY} and record the agreed brief in {DOCS}. The editor and sound effects editor jointly clarify creative intent and technical constraints.
tasks.previous_blocker: A cue list alone does not resolve creative meaning or production tradeoffs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication already supports the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: The desired effect may be hard to explain or technically impractical.
tasks.human_edge: Use examples and questions to reach a shared understanding of the intended sound.
tasks.altitude: Discussion time and creative responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate the sound brief into technical requirements

evidence.claim: Creative sound-requirement discussion remains human; the digest's rough-cut tools do not establish shorter collaborative sound decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is discussing and agreeing sound requirements, not asset generation or insertion. Any initial cue decision under4055 is counted once; existing sound editor participation remains outside and unchanged.

Film editor supplies current cut/version, cue locations and intended effect before discussing each item; sound effects editor supplies feasibility and alternatives during the discussion before agreement. Clarification and brief capture are included in retained100 hours. No free structured approved-sound flag is assumed; unresolved items remain questions.
Native communication and document tools precede custom workflows; no new participant capture task is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the process and tools are unchanged.
